source.title: Studying Image Tokenizers as Visual Languages in Unified Multimodal Models
source.authors: Siting Li; Zheng-Yang Wang; S. Du; Xi Chen; Yang Liu

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends loss-scaling analysis to unified multimodal continual pretraining and reports its own validation-loss results, but does not conduct a full compute-scaling-law or compute-optimal-frontier study.
record.gate_note: The paper measures task-specific validation losses while varying data and model size, and relates losses to downstream generation and understanding scores. It does not derive small-run extrapolations or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. It cites prior language-model scaling results, but those cited results are not extracted as rows. Tokenizer design comparisons unrelated to scaling or loss–performance prediction are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study reports held-out loss against data and model size for mixed image–text continual pretraining of Qwen3 (0.6B–4B), and correlates pretraining loss with post-SFT benchmarks. That bears on V1, V5, V6 and V7 in a new setting. It fits no exponents, makes no extrapolation and finds no compute-optimal split. The sweeps span under one order of magnitude (data ×4, params ×~7).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but scaling-centred. The authors' main conclusion concerns tokenizers. Task-specific losses scale differently and must be analysed per task. I2T loss is a consistent cross-tokenizer signal of post-SFT generation and general VQA, while T2I loss shifts with the token space. Reconstruction fidelity can diverge from multimodal learnability, and the image tokenizer can affect text modelling. They explicitly disclaim a full scaling-law study or compute-efficient frontiers.
record.recipe_differences: Uses held-out task-specific cross-entropy during mixed-modal continual pretraining from pretrained Qwen3 backbones, rather than the original language-model scaling-law setups. It varies model size and data in limited sweeps, does not derive compute-optimal allocations, and examines tokenizer-dependent multimodal losses.
record.method_sensitivity: Loss behavior depends on task and hyperparameters (learning rate and batch size); annealing mainly reduces text loss while leaving image-side losses largely unchanged. Data-scaling curves also show task- and tokenizer-dependent curvature.

fits_no_version.finding: Image tokenizer choice changes text-loss difficulty under joint training, via the image-token prediction objective (Fig 10, Fig 22).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In unified multimodal models, the visual token space affects text-modeling loss through cross-modal interference.

record.problems: The reported scaling ranges are limited, and the authors explicitly do not conduct a full scaling-law study or derive compute-efficient frontiers. Main scaling curves are presented primarily in plots, with no uncertainty estimates reported for them. The results use one backbone family (Qwen3); most central experiments use one data-shuffling seed, with a two-seed check only for one GigaTok configuration.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted tokenizer reconstruction and design ablations, including Table 3 and Figures 10–14, because they do not directly test the listed scaling, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, architecture-shape, or loss-to-downstream-predictability versions. Also omitted supplementary tokenizer entropy and PMI diagnostics (Figures 11–12 and Tables 9–10), which do not measure those claim versions.

untested.parts: Power law over several orders of magnitude; training from scratch; token-count scaling with separate runs; fitted exponents.
All: no small-run fits extrapolated to larger runs.
All: no depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count.
Video or other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning/transfer scaling, from-scratch multimodal training, other backbone families, ranges beyond 0.6B–4B and 12M–48M samples.
Downstream improvement as a direct function of scale; tasks beyond GenAI, MJHQ, VQAv2, GQA and TextVQA.
Parameter-counting conventions, fitting method, exponent estimates, sensitivity of the compute-optimal split.

missing.what: Within-GigaTok correlations of T2I and I2T loss with GenAI and MJHQ: pretraining r=-0.954/+0.956 (T2I), -0.917/+0.885 (I2T); post-SFT -0.918/+0.973 (T2I), -0.883/+0.900 (I2T).
Cross-tokenizer T2I loss–performance: unnormalized r=+0.016 (R²=0) vs log2B-normalized r=-0.957 across IBQ variants; tokenizer-dependent shifts.
Annealed vs non-annealed loss–FLOPs: annealing mainly reduces text loss, and lr=1e-4 gains more from annealing.
4B UniTok-sem loss curve including earlier checkpoints, with quadratic coefficients (e.g. text a=-6.995e-03).
Loss scaling across JourneyDB and BLIP3o image sources.

record.verdict_notes: The data-scaling points are checkpoints from a single run per configuration under a WSD constant phase, not independent data budgets. Model-size scaling changes the pretrained backbone. The record swapped the R11 and R12 values. The Fig 9 subjects span seven tokenizers, not GigaTok. One data-shuffling seed, with only a two-seed check.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests data and model-size scaling in a mixed-modal continual-pretraining setup, but covers less than an order of magnitude in the reported sweeps; it does not establish the claim over several orders of magnitude or test language-only pretraining from scratch.
No test of fitting power laws on small runs and predicting runs orders of magnitude larger.
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation sweep, stable allocation exponents, or comparison of parameter and token growth with compute.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.

Tests one setting: discrete-image-tokenizer unified autoregressive multimodal continual pretraining from Qwen3. Does not test other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer as scaling regimes, or other backbone families.
Tests associations between pretraining losses and selected post-SFT generation and visual-question-answering benchmarks; does not establish downstream predictability for other tasks or modalities.

Tests some sensitivity to task, learning rate, batch size, annealing, and curve shape. Does not compare parameter-counting conventions, derive fitted scaling exponents, or test compute-optimal allocation sensitivity.

rows.operation_detail: Quadratic fits to data-scaling loss curves.

conditions.value: Intermediate, pre-annealing checkpoints from individual runs
GigaTok, GigaTok-DINO, IBQ-1024, IBQ-8192, IBQ-16384, UniTok, UniTok-sem

rows.measure: Quadratic coefficient of validation loss against data scale; positive coefficients indicate convexity and negative coefficients concavity.
rows.value: Most I2T, T2I, and image data-scaling curves are convex; text curves are mostly slightly concave. Table 8 reports different quadratic coefficients by tokenizer and task.
rows.note: The paper also describes the principal curves as roughly power-law-like; quadratic-fit curvature indicates departures in shape, not a complete rejection of that description.
rows.check: Each quadratic is fitted to only three checkpoints (12M/24M/48M) from one run, so it is a weak curvature test. Text curves are slightly concave and image-side curves convex (e.g. GigaTok-DINO Caption a=-7.73e-03). This bears on single-power-law shape for V1 and V5 as well as V7.

conditions.value: Grid includes 1e-4 and 3e-5, among other tested settings

rows.measure: Task-specific validation losses over data scale and hyperparameter settings.
rows.value: No hyperparameter setting dominates all tasks: aggressive settings favor I2T, T2I, and image losses, while milder settings maintain better text fitting; the text and image-related tasks favor different settings.
rows.note: This is evidence of setup sensitivity in observed loss trends, not an estimate of scaling exponents.
rows.check: The grid in Fig 19 has eight (lr,bs) settings, including lr=1e-5. The row shows loss levels and trends differ by setting and task, not fitted exponents.
